note: Jev questions sent with every review. state = review_text only (no stars, dates or versions). Code maps answers into the common schema.

topic.instructions: Which part of the Spotify app is this review mainly about? If several problems are mentioned, pick the most serious one; if equally serious, the first one mentioned. For a positive review, pick the first specific feature praised; general praise is other. Mentioning a paid plan alone is not billing.

criteria.access: Login, signup, password or account access problems
criteria.usability: Navigation, controls, layout, queue or playlist management, ad interruptions and ad frequency
criteria.playback: Music fails to play, app crashes or will not open, lag, connection failures, audio quality, battery or data use
criteria.downloads: Downloading songs, saved music, offline listening, downloads disappearing
criteria.catalog: Missing songs or artists, search and discovery, recommendations, lyrics availability
criteria.billing: Price, charges, subscriptions, paywalls, premium entitlement, and controls that are explicitly premium only (skip limits, forced shuffle, choosing songs, lyrics locked behind premium)
criteria.support: Contacting Spotify support and the support response
criteria.other: General praise or criticism with no specific feature, unrelated content, or no supported specific topic

intent.instructions: What is the writer doing in this review?

criteria.cancellation: Explicitly says they are leaving, uninstalling, cancelling, switching apps, or threatening to do so
criteria.complaint: Describes a negative experience, including mixed praise and criticism, or generic statements like bad app
criteria.request: Asks for a change or new feature without reporting a failure
criteria.unclear: Meaningless or unrelated text, or a bare boycott slogan with no product complaint and no personal departure

severity.instructions: How bad is the problem the writer reports? Judge only the reported impact, not angry language, stars or cancellation threats. Do not invent impact that is not stated.

criteria.1: No reported problem: praise, neutral or unclear content, or a pure feature request
criteria.2: Dislike, generic criticism, minor annoyance or cosmetic issue, with no stated loss of function
criteria.3: A function is degraded or restricted but some use or a workaround remains
criteria.4: A core task is clearly blocked, such as being unable to log in, open the app, or play music
criteria.5: Explicit serious financial, privacy or data harm, such as being charged wrongly or losing data; an expensive plan, a crash or angry language alone is not enough

sentiment.instructions: What is the overall tone of the review toward Spotify?

leaving.instructions: Does the writer explicitly say they are leaving, uninstalling, cancelling, switching to another app, or threatening to do so?

criteria.true: An explicit personal statement or threat of departure, e.g. 'uninstalling', 'bye Spotify', 'I'm leaving', 'switching to YouTube Music'
criteria.false: No explicit departure; general anger, low stars or a boycott slogan without a personal departure

code_rules.sentiment: score / 2 - 1, rounded to 2 decimals (0..4 maps to -1..1)
code_rules.intent_precedence: if leaving >= LEAVING_THRESHOLD then cancellation; else Jev intent choice; order cancellation > complaint > request > praise > unclear
code_rules.needs_review: true when any of: topic confidence < 0.5, severity confidence < 0.5, leaving between 0.2 and 0.8
code_rules.evidence_quote: whole review if 200 characters or fewer; otherwise Jev picks one of the review's own sentences (extra Choice question in the same request); code checks it is an exact substring. Haiku writes the quote only for capped fallback cases.
code_rules.entities: code keyword list, kept only when the term appears in the text (config/entities.json)

quote.instructions: Which sentence of the review best shows the main reported problem, or the main praised feature if there is no problem? This is the sentence that decides the topic.
quote.criteria: built per review by code: s1..sN = the review's own sentences, split on sentence punctuation and line breaks
